claim: Tens of thousands of civilians, including children, have been killed in Gaza.

heard.who: Gaza Health Ministry, as reported by the Associated Press (PBS), June 2025
heard.quote: The ministry says 55,104 people have been killed since the start of the war and 127,394 wounded.

heard.who: UN humanitarian agency OCHA, citing the Gaza Health Ministry, as reported by NPR (OPB), May 2024
heard.quote: says 7,797 children and 4,959 women were killed in Gaza as of April 30

answer: Many civilians, including thousands of children, have been killed in Gaza. Nobody has published an independent count of how many of the dead were fighters. The main total comes from the Gaza Health Ministry, part of the Hamas-run government, which counts bodies reaching hospitals and does not separate civilians from fighters. The UN treats the total as reliable overall. In May 2024 the UN broke down only the fully identified dead: 7,797 children and 4,959 women by 30 April 2024. Two Lancet studies estimated the ministry undercounted. Israel says it killed more than 20,000 militants, without evidence. A parent can say: tens of thousands have been killed, the share who were civilians is disputed, and no count is settled.

facts.text: The Gaza Health Ministry, part of Gaza's Hamas-run government, counts deaths from the bodies that reach hospitals and morgues, supplemented since the early months with media reports and first responders. Its totals never distinguish between civilians and combatants.

facts.text: Despite the revision, the UN kept treating the ministry's overall total as reliable. The Associated Press found that in earlier wars the ministry's counts held up to UN and Israeli checks, and Reuters reports that Israel's military has accepted in briefings that the overall numbers are broadly reliable.

facts.text: Two peer-reviewed studies estimated that the ministry undercounted. A 2025 Lancet capture-recapture study estimated 64,260 deaths from traumatic injury to 30 June 2024 (95% interval 55,298 to 78,525), putting the ministry's count about 41 percent below the estimate (the estimate is about 70 percent above the ministry's 37,877). A 2026 Lancet Global Health household survey estimated 75,200 violent deaths to 5 January 2025, with the ministry's figure of 49,090 34.7 percent below that. Neither study estimates how many of the dead were fighters.

facts.text: Israel does not give a verified count of combatants killed. It put the figure at 17,000-18,000 in 2024 and says recent assessments are about 20,000, with about one civilian killed per fighter; in May 2024 the prime minister said the ratio was almost 1 to 1. None of this was accompanied by evidence.

facts.text: The UN human rights office verified 8,119 deaths from the first months of the war, each with at least three sources; 44 percent were children and 26 percent women. This is a verified subset of the ministry's reported toll, not a full count and not a split between fighters and civilians.

facts.text: A joint investigation by The Guardian, +972 Magazine and Local Call reported in August 2025 that an Israeli military intelligence database listed 8,900 named Hamas and Palestinian Islamic Jihad fighters as dead or probably dead by May 2025, about 17 percent of the 53,000 deaths then reported. CBC said it had not seen the data; the Israeli army did not dispute that the database exists. This is one report, based on documents not independently verified.

facts.text: Researchers disagree on whether the ministry's figures are fabricated. Abraham Wyner, a Wharton statistician, argued in Tablet that the daily totals for 26 October to 10 November 2023 varied too little (about 270 a day, plus or minus about 15 percent) to be natural. Other researchers found no sign of inflation: UNRWA staff deaths compared with ministry totals made fabrication implausible, and a capture-recapture study found the ministry under-reported by 41 percent.

sources.quote: the daily reported casualty count over this period averages 270 plus or minus about 15%. This is strikingly little variation.

sources.quote: suggesting the Palestinian MoH under-reported mortality by 41%

contested.text: The share of the dead who were civilians is the most disputed figure, and the ministry does not give it. The Associated Press analysed the ministry's data and called the share of women and children 'the best available proxy for civilian casualties'; it found that share fell from above 60 percent in October 2023 to below 40 percent in April 2024. A proxy is not a civilian count.

sources.title: Women and children of Gaza are being killed less frequently as war's toll rises, AP analysis finds
sources.quote: the death rate for women and children is the best available proxy for civilian casualties in one of the 21st century's most destructive conflicts.

contested.text: The ministry is part of the Hamas-run government, which is why its figures are questioned. An Israeli army spokesman said in May 2024 that the military does not know how many civilians have been killed, and that Hamas does not either (NBC News). In October 2023 Israel said the ministry inflated the toll of a deadly explosion, after the ministry reported 500 dead and then lowered it to 471, while US intelligence agencies estimated 100 to 300 (AP).

not_claimed: This card does not say any single count is settled or exact.
It does not say all those killed were civilians, and it does not say most were fighters.
It does not deny that many civilians, including children, were killed.
It does not say how many of the dead were killed by Israeli forces and how many by other causes.
could_not_verify: I looked for an independent count of fighters among the dead and found none. The closest are the UN human rights office's verified subset (age and sex only) and a Guardian, +972 Magazine and Local Call report of a leaked Israeli database, which I could only read through CBC and Middle East Eye (the original was not readable) and which is not independently verified.

I could not find a reliable outlet or academic paper that examined Wyner's method in reply; the other scholarly checks (UNRWA staff comparison, capture-recapture, household survey) test the same question but are not direct replies to him. Jerusalem Post, JNS and Jewish Exponent pieces on Wyner repeat the Tablet article and are not counted as separate sources.
The Huynh, Chin and Spiegel Lancet letter of December 2023 (UNRWA staff deaths compared with the ministry's) could not be read; it is cited only through Khatib, McKee and Yusuf.
The OHCHR press release or report on the 8,119 verified deaths could not be fetched; it is cited from Al Jazeera, Reuters (via CBC) and LBC.
The method behind Israel's fighter counts (17,000-18,000 or 20,000) was not found in any source.

answer_claims.says: Many civilians, including thousands of children, have been killed in Gaza.
Nobody has published an independent count of how many of the dead were fighters.
The main total comes from the Gaza Health Ministry, part of the Hamas-run government, which counts bodies reaching hospitals and does not separate civilians from fighters.
The UN treats the total as reliable overall.
In May 2024 the UN broke down only the fully identified dead: 7,797 children and 4,959 women by 30 April 2024.
Two Lancet studies estimated the ministry undercounted.
Israel says it killed more than 20,000 militants, without evidence.
A parent can say: tens of thousands have been killed, the share who were civilians is disputed, and no count is settled.

skeptic.notes: Read 2+ sources per fact in context (CBC/AP, PBS/AP, RNZ/Reuters, OPB/NPR, OCHA, CBC, Al Jazeera, VOA, NBC, JNS, JPost). Quotes are on the pages. Fixed: fact 3 said the Lancet estimate was '41 percent above the ministry's figure'; 64,260 is about 70 percent above 37,877, and the 41 percent is the ministry's shortfall as a share of the estimate; reworded. Fact 0 said the total comes from hospital and morgue records only; the PBS page also names the Red Crescent and the Lancet reports a family survey; reworded and added that Hamas controls the ministry (page says so). Independence: [must-fix] fact 5 (Wyner) is three outlets (JPost, JNS, Jewish Exponent) all reporting one Tablet article, i.e. one source; the writer could not read Tablet. [should-fix] fact 0 and fact 2 are AP twice (CBC, PBS) plus one other (Reuters, NPR), so two independent sources, not three. Strongest objection from critics of Israel (stronger): the card gives Israel's '20,000 militants / 1 to 1' claims a fact but omits any independent breakdown of the dead into fighters and civilians (the card's own could_not_verify says none was found; I did not search beyond the cited pages for a report on Israel's internal records, which the writer should do); I could only add proxies from pages already cited (Lancet 59.1 percent women, children and elderly; UN analysis of 8,000 verified deaths, 44 percent children) to contested. Strongest objection from defenders: the ministry is run under Hamas control and its figures were disputed early (Israel said it inflated a hospital-explosion toll; US intelligence gave a lower figure): added to contested from the PBS page already cited. Both numbers are labelled by who counted. No graphic content. [should-fix] Add a fact for the AP 'women and children share fell' finding (one source today) and for Israel's own fighter database if a reliable report exists. [nit] contested[1] and [5] (AP proxy; L'Orient Today) are plain strings because their pages are not sources on this card.

citer.notes: Every sentence now ties to a fact. Changed only the last sentence: 'the share who were civilians is disputed, and no single count is settled' was not carried by a fact (fact 4 gives only Israel's unevidenced claim and nothing on the card gives a civilian share); it now says the ministry does not say how many were civilians and Israel's fighter figure has no evidence shown. Fact 0 now carries 'part of the Hamas-run government'. 'Many civilians, including thousands of children' rests on fact 1 (ministry-identified deaths, counted by OCHA); that is a ministry count, and the answer names the ministry. Converted 4 of 6 contested entries to {text, sources}; contested[1] (AP 'best available proxy', PBS June 2024) and [5] (L'Orient Today) have no source on this card, so they stay strings and block verification. Dropped from contested[0] the Sept 2025 figure (Channels TV, not a source here) and from [2] Omar Shakir (no page).
